case.paper_title: The Ideological Congruence Controversy: The Impact of Alternative Measures, Data, and Time Periods on the Effects of Election Rules
case.focal_claim: Under SMD (single member district) election rules, party competition should lead the plurality vote winner to be close to the median voter. (p. 1484.)
case.hypothesis: Using the operationalized Manifesto-method distance between the plurality vote winner and the median voter, SMD elections should have smaller plurality-winner distance from the median voter than PR elections.

tasks_info.task_instruction: You should use the data from 1945-2003. You should use the Manifesto Method instead of the Cit-Expert and Method in your analysis.
tasks_info.task_goal: Produce one statistical result comparable to the original paper's focal result.

conclusion_rule.statistical_threshold: For a frequentist result, p <= 0.05 is affirmative support; 0.05 < p <= 0.055 is borderline support only if the estimate is substantively meaningful and the uncertainty interval narrowly crosses the null.
conclusion_rule.support_rule: For a frequentist result, support requires the expected direction with p <= 0.05, or borderline evidence with 0.05 < p <= 0.055 when the estimate is substantively meaningful and the uncertainty interval narrowly crosses the null. Borderline support remains support. Clearly weak aligned evidence is inconclusive. Opposite requires affirmative evidence of a material contrary effect.

plan.path_summary: Estimate the SMD-vs-PR contrast in the median Manifesto-method plurality-winner distance from the median voter using median quantile regression, preserving the raw distance outcome and binary election-rule contrast while changing the model estimand from the earlier mean-based OLS path.

path_signature.sample_restriction: Task1: rows with election rule coded smd or pr and nonmissing focal variables. Task2: years 1945-2003 inclusive, rows with election rule coded smd or pr, and nonmissing focal variables.
path_signature.missing_data_rule: Listwise deletion for the required analysis columns in each task: Task1 uses smd, pldist1, and year; Task2 uses year, smd, and pldist1.
path_signature.variable_construction: Clean smd labels to lowercase; create smd_bin=1 for smd and 0 for pr; use pldist1 in raw units as the Manifesto-method plurality-winner distance.
path_signature.inference_rule: Expected direction is negative. Support requires a negative SMD coefficient with p <= 0.05, or borderline support for 0.05 < p <= 0.055 when the estimate is substantively meaningful and the interval narrowly crosses zero. A positive coefficient is opposite only with affirmative p < 0.05 evidence and an interval above zero; otherwise inconclusive.

analysis_path.path_description: Use all authorized observations with smd or pr election-rule coding and estimate whether SMD elections have a lower median Manifesto-method plurality-winner distance from the median voter than PR elections.
preprocessing_steps: Validate that columns smd, pldist1, and year exist.
Create smd_clean by converting smd to lowercase stripped strings.
Keep only observations with smd_clean equal to smd or pr; report rows removed.
Drop observations missing pldist1, smd_clean, or year; report rows removed.
Create smd_bin equal to 1 for smd and 0 for pr.
Fit median quantile regression pldist1 ~ smd_bin.
Report the coefficient, standard error, p-value, 95% confidence interval, direction, conclusion class, sample flow, and group summaries.

models.planned_estimation: Coefficient on smd_bin, interpreted as the SMD-minus-PR difference in the conditional median Manifesto-method plurality-winner distance.
models.inference_criteria: Support for the focal claim requires the smd_bin coefficient to be negative with p <= 0.05, or borderline negative evidence with 0.05 < p <= 0.055 when the interval narrowly crosses zero; opposite requires an affirmative positive effect.
models.qualification: The focal claim uses language of closeness and the observed pldist1 distribution is skewed with values from approximately 0 to 59. A median raw-scale contrast is a defensible robustness analysis that preserves the focal outcome and contrast while reducing dependence on the mean.

method_justification.claim_alignment: Both tasks directly test whether plurality winners are closer to the median voter under SMD by estimating the SMD-minus-PR contrast in pldist1. A negative contrast maps to the focal claim.
method_justification.dataset_alignment: Both tasks use only the authorized data/powell_original.dta file and verified columns. Task2 explicitly uses the 1945-2003 Manifesto-method pldist1 variable.
method_justification.method_reason: Median quantile regression is appropriate for a continuous distance outcome and a binary election-rule predictor when the substantive claim is about closeness and the inspected distance distribution is skewed. It preserves the raw outcome and focal contrast while avoiding unsupported controls or sample changes.
method_justification.novelty_reason: Shared Memory path01 used mean-based OLS for pldist1 on smd_bin, with decade fixed effects for Task1 and a simple raw mean difference for Task2. This path changes only the model estimand to median quantile regression, preserving outcome, contrast, sample, and inference rules where possible.
